questions.q: How do you say « there are ten books » ?
questions.why: Il y a is frozen: the il is not a real subject and nothing agrees with what follows. Singular or plural, the form is identical.

questions.q: Imperfect: ___ beaucoup de monde. (there were a lot of people)
questions.why: Only the avoir part changes across the tenses. The imperfect describes a scene or an ongoing state.
Avoir's future stem is aur-, so il y a becomes il y aura. The conditional, il y aurait, follows the same stem.

questions.q: « ___ un accident. » Which form fits a single event that happened?
questions.why: Il y a eu is the passé composé, for one completed event. Il y avait would describe an ongoing scene instead.

questions.q: Make it negative: « Il y a un problème. » → ___
a: Il n'y a pas de problème
Il n'y a pas de problème.
il n'y a pas de problème
questions.why: Ne wraps the a, y stays put, and the indefinite un collapses to de after the negative.

questions.q: Make it negative: « Il y a quelqu'un. » → ___ (There's nobody.)
questions.why: Personne and rien replace pas outright — never « ne … pas personne ». The parallel is « Il n'y a rien » for quelque chose.

questions.q: Build the formal question: Is there a problem?
questions.why: Inversion gives « Y a-t-il un problème ? » with the -t- inserted for sound. Neutral is « Est-ce qu'il y a… » and spoken is just « Il y a un problème ? »

questions.q: In conversation, « Il y a » is normally reduced to what?
questions.why: Speech drops the il: « Y a un problème ? », « Y a personne », « Y a pas de quoi. » Understand it, but write the full form.

questions.q: il y a or depuis? J'habite ici ___ deux ans. (and I still do)
questions.why: Depuis + present means the situation is still true. Il y a + a duration means ago, and takes a past tense.

questions.q: il y a or depuis? Je l'ai vu ___ une heure. (an hour ago)
questions.why: Followed by a duration, il y a means ago and points at a finished moment. The past tense of the verb is the giveaway.

questions.q: Which sentence does NOT mean « I've lived here for two years » ?
choices: Il y a deux ans que j'habite ici
Ça fait deux ans que j'habite ici
Il y a deux ans, j'ai habité ici
questions.why: Il y a … que behaves like depuis and keeps the present tense. Without que, il y a plus a past tense means ago: two years ago I lived here.

questions.q: Say this out loud, in the full written form.
questions.why: Rien replaces pas in the negative. In speech the whole thing collapses towards « y a rien », but the written form keeps il and ne.

questions.q: Explain the difference between « il y a », « voilà » and « c'est », with an example of each.
a: Il y a states that something exists, introducing something new: Il y a un restaurant dans la rue. Voilà points at something: Voilà le restaurant ! C'est identifies something already in view: — Il y a quelqu'un ? — Oui, c'est moi.
questions.why: The three are not interchangeable: existence, pointing, identifying. A natural exchange uses il y a to introduce and c'est to identify.

questions.q: « Il ne faut pas fumer ici » means:
choices: You don't have to smoke here
questions.why: Il ne faut pas is a prohibition, not an absence of obligation. For « you don't have to », say tu n'es pas obligé de or ce n'est pas nécessaire de.
Il reste means there is … left, one of the impersonal expressions built like il y a, alongside il manque and il faut.

questions.q: Build the sentence: I arrived two hours ago.
questions.why: Il y a plus a length of time means ago, and it follows the verb. Depuis would mean I am still arriving, which is nonsense.

questions.q: Build the sentence: There was nobody there.
questions.why: Il y avait is the imperfect, for a scene rather than an event. Personne closes the sentence and needs no pas.
